gm_ratio=0.582 (heavy gradient loss) vs spectral_slope_ratio=1.041 (only mild steepening) is inconsistent with isotropic gaussian. final_decision.rationale: Single-step anisotropic motion blur at severity 1 (radius=5, sigma=3). No compression (block_boundary 0.987<1.05, unique_G 238/254), no global (variance_ratio 0.992, mean_shift -0.4, chroma 0.992), no noise (wavelet sigma 0.74; 6-step check all explained by blur residual; noiseless motion:1 simulation reproduces target noise-step fingerprint exactly). Verdict UNCERTAIN rather than LIKELY because blur_motion samples a random angle, so PSNR cannot exceed 40 dB even with correct pipeline (SKILL C4), and best observed PSNR is 34.49 dB (30-40 band). reflection_R1.method: signal re-interpretation (not residual diagnosis): reran run_full_analysis on pair0 (full_analysis_R1.json), ran peeled_noise_check with the R0 pipeline (peeled_noise_R1.json), ran run_full_analysis on clean-vs-clean as a compression baseline, and ran run_full_analysis on a fresh noiseless blur_motion:1 simulation (full_analysis_sim_motion1_pair0_R1.json) as a full-fingerprint control.

signal_reinterpretation.finding: Logic artifact. run_full_analysis sets has_noise = (step2.verdict != 'NO_NOISE'); the low-confidence GAUSSIAN_YCrCb label (sigma=0.74) forced has_noise=True, so blur was judged by slope_ratio 1.041<1.08 instead of the pure-blur branch gm_ratio<0.62 (0.582 would have PASSED). Control: clean-vs-clean also returns step2 IMPULSE with sigma=0.0 -> has_noise=True, confirming the verdict-string coupling. Blur presence is real.

Not measurements. step3_blur returns early at BLUR_UNLIKELY (run_full_analysis.py lines 526-535); residual_anisotropy/glass_score/blur_PCA (lines 542-600) are never computed. The 0.00/0.0 values are uncomputed defaults echoed by the summary. They never contradicted motion and must not be used as evidence.

Blur-confounded. clean baseline 0.2785; noiseless blur_motion:1 simulation 0.5675 (>= target). Near-zero 8x8 AC coefficients rise under smoothing. block_boundary target 0.9873 vs clean 0.9828 vs sim 0.9897 -> no 8x8 grid (0% FP rule; far below 1.05). No JPEG step.
Blur averaging. Noiseless motion:1 sim unique_G=238 (ratio 0.937), per-channel [240,238,239] vs target [242,239,238]. No quantization.

Joint signature excludes deterministic isotropic blur: gaussian sev1-4 max PSNR 32.21 dB and lens sev1-3 max 32.15 dB are deterministic functions and never exceeded 40 dB -> exact-match ruled out. deterministic -> stable PSNR; ceiling <40 dB rules out exact match (R0 data)

support_validation.interpretation: blur_motion samples a random angle per call; CI 10/10 on 4/5 pairs and a 65.91 dB pixel-level reproduction on pair3 confirm subtype+severity. R0 pair values (22.69-34.49 dB) and R1 values (25.44-65.91 dB) sample the same angle-driven distribution.

final_decision.rationale: R1 signal re-interpretation resolved the boundary/contradictory signals in favor of the R0 pipeline: BLUR_UNLIKELY was a has_noise-verdict artifact, anisotropy/PCA were never computed, dct/unique_G are blur-induced, noise and global fingerprints are fully reproduced by a noiseless motion:1 simulation. Fresh 5-pair validation produced CI 10/10 on 4/5 pairs and 65.91 dB on pair3 (aligned random angle) - a near pixel-exact reproduction that no alternative and no extra step can achieve. Verdict remains UNCERTAIN per SKILL C4 because the random angle makes PSNR draw-dependent.
